answer: Sybil resistance comes from slot-rent auctions. The protocol anchors each identity to one of S fixed rent slots, valid only while it prepays clearing rent set by sealed-bid auction. Honest agents keep a cheap oasis at floor bid. A sybil buying n identities outbids itself: slot k costs base*(1+k/S), the clearing price climbs like a ridge, so total cost is base*n*n/(2S), superlinear in n. Miners refuse any signature whose rent lapsed below the clearing price; lapsed deposits burn after a 7-day time-lock, and each slot binds one key and one cooldown, blocking parallel reset.
